key_insight: Inline hyperspectral imaging can separate donor and acceptor signals during roll-to-roll slot-die coating, enabling real-time mapping of active-layer composition and aggregation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical metrology tool for scalable organic photovoltaic manufacturing by supporting quality control directly on the production line.
method: Hyperspectral camera monitors P3HT and OIDTBR coatings in a roll-to-roll slot-die setup.
Multivariate curve resolution extracts the spatial distribution of donor and acceptor contributions.
Spectral fitting of P3HT absorbance maps exciton bandwidth to probe polymer aggregation and chain interactions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful resolution of donor/acceptor spatial distributions and mapping of P3HT exciton bandwidth from inline spectral data.
watch_item: Industrial deployment will depend on robust calibration and spectral unmixing under varying coating speeds, thicknesses, and process noise.
paper_title: Hyperspectral imaging for inline quality monitoring of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers
